original_metadata.title: A transitive topological groupoid with smooth base, first-countable arrow space and manifold source fibers and isotropy groups has a unique compatible Lie groupoid up to a base-preserving continuous isomorphism
original_metadata.author: Pawel Razny
original_metadata.source_title: The Solution of Hilbert's Fifth Problem  for Transitive Groupoids
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: Smoothness of the base and local Euclidean isotropy do not by themselves give the missing quotient-map hypothesis for a groupoid. The author controls the source-fiber orbit space through Cartan principal bundles, covering dimension and local product neighborhoods. The invariance-of-domain argument establishes the crucial local Euclidean structure and target quotient property before the established smoothing theorem can apply.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete new Section3 proof, both dimension/product lemmas and all Cartan-bundle definitions and cited hypotheses were read. The author identifies the source-fiber orbit space, proves its Hausdorff/local-compact/second-countable properties, applies established Cartan local triviality and invariant-metric dimension results, and then uses a compact-neighborhood comparison plus invariance of domain to show this orbit space is locally Euclidean. The resulting target restriction is a quotient map. The prior, explicitly stated Theorem1.1 then supplies the Lie-groupoid smoothing and uniqueness; that prior theorem is background, while removal of its quotient-map assumption is the new complete local core. Separate Gleason-Yamabe quotient variants are not counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem3.6 for a transitive topological groupoid G with smooth base G0, first-countable arrow space G1, and topological-manifold source fiber G_x and isotropy group G_x^x (equivalently all fibers/isotropy groups by transitivity). The conclusion is a continuously isomorphic compatible Lie groupoid unique through base-preserving isomorphism as in the source. The quotient property of t_x is proved, not an extra hypothesis. Standard Hausdorff/second-countable manifold conventions used in the dimension proof are retained. No weakening to a merely topological base, arbitrary non-manifold isotropy or nontransitive groupoid is asserted.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The full original main Theorem 3.6 and complete author local quotient-map proof are retained, together with all topological/groupoid/Cartan-bundle context and the two new dimension/product lemmas. The source-fiber orbit-space separation/compactness/metric dimension, relatively compact neighborhood comparison and invariance-of-domain argument establish local Euclidean structure and the target quotient property. Prior Lie-groupoid smoothing/uniqueness is explicitly credited background Theorem 1.1. The theorem is author-positioned as the main removal of its formerly extra quotient-map assumption, with the complete new core bundled into one unit. Source Hausdorff/second-countable manifold conventions are included; Gleason–Yamabe variants are not counted.
